html:
The settlement by Greeks of the Aegean islands and the west coast of Anatolia in the Greek Dark Ages, from about the 11th to the 9th century BCE. The central part of that coast became known as Ionia.

Greek tradition said that after the fall of the Mycenaean kingdoms the Ionians gathered in Athens and sailed east under the sons of King Codrus. Neleus founded Miletus and Androclus founded Ephesus. Archaeology confirms that Greek speaking settlers arrived in these places in the centuries after the collapse of Mycenaean Greece, though the story of a single migration is a later simplification.

Twelve Ionian cities later formed the Ionian League, including Miletus, Ephesus, Samos, Chios and Phocaea. Trading with Lydia and the Near East, they became the richest part of the Greek world. Ionia gave birth to Greek philosophy with Thales, and its revolt against Persia in 499 BCE, the Ionian Revolt, set off the Persian Wars.
sum: The settlement by Greeks of the Aegean islands and the west coast of Anatolia in the Greek Dark Ages, from about the 11th to the 9th century BCE. The central part of that coast became known as Ionia.
